title: How a brain learns
blurb: Meet the neuron — the tiny piece behind ChatGPT and friends. Then watch one teach itself.

steps.title: The AI behind the headlines
steps.body:
Chatbots that write essays, apps that make art — almost all of them run on **neural networks**.

They sound scary and brainy. They're not. A neural network is built from a tiny, simple part called a **neuron**, and by the end you'll have trained one yourself.

steps.title: What's a neuron?
steps.body:
Your brain has billions of brain cells (neurons) that pass along little signals. Scientists borrowed the idea and made a **digital neuron**.

A digital neuron is just a tiny decision-maker: it takes a few numbers in, weighs them up, and makes one simple call — **yes or no**, this group or that one.

steps.title: Weights: how much it listens
steps.body:
Each input to a neuron has a **weight** — a knob for *how much that input matters*.

Big weight = "I really care about this input." Small or negative weight = "meh, ignore it" or "count it against." Tuning those weights is the *entire* secret to making a neuron smart.

steps.title: It draws a line
steps.body:
When a neuron has two inputs, its decision is literally a **line** on a graph: everything on one side is "Group A," everything on the other is "Group B."

The weights **tilt and slide** that line. Let's grab the knobs.

steps.title: Tilt the line
steps.body: Move the Weight and Bias sliders to get the line between the two groups. Get to 100% — then try the 'Let it learn' button!

steps.title: You just set the weights by hand
steps.body:
Fiddling those sliders to separate the groups? That was you doing the neuron's job for it.

With only three knobs it's doable. But real networks have **millions** of weights — nobody could set those by hand. So here's the breakthrough…

steps.title: It can tune *itself*
steps.body:
Press **Let it learn** and watch. The neuron checks each dot, sees which ones it got wrong, and nudges its own weights a little to fix them — over and over, until the line snaps into place.

That self-tuning loop is the heartbeat of *all* modern AI.

steps.title: What is 'learning'?
steps.question: When a neural network "learns," what is actually changing inside it?
steps.explain: Learning = adjusting the weights. Every AI you've heard of is just doing this, on a massive scale.

steps.title: One neuron, one line
steps.body:
A single neuron can only draw **one straight line**. That's great for two tidy groups — but real problems are messier than a straight line can handle.

So what do we do? The same thing nature did: use **lots** of neurons together.

steps.title: Many neurons = a network
steps.body:
Connect many neurons in **layers** and something amazing happens: their simple lines combine into **curves and complex shapes**. Now the network can recognize faces, understand sentences, or generate images.

The word *deep* in "deep learning" just means *many layers* of these neurons.

steps.title: Why so many?
steps.question: Why stack lots of neurons into a network instead of using just one?
choices: So they can learn complex patterns a single straight line can't
steps.explain: One neuron = one line. Many neurons together can bend and combine into the complex patterns real problems need.

steps.title: Same idea, gigantic scale
steps.body:
The AI that chats with you? A neural network with **billions** of weights, trained on a huge chunk of the internet.

But peek inside and it's the exact thing you just did: neurons, weights, and a learning loop that nudges the weights to be a little less wrong. You now understand the core of the most powerful AI on Earth.

steps.title: Big recap
steps.question: What do a tiny neuron and a giant chatbot have in common?
choices: Both learn by adjusting weights to lower their mistakes
steps.explain: Same core idea at wildly different sizes: adjust the weights, lower the error, repeat.

steps.title: You did it — the whole journey 🎉
steps.body:
Look how far you came:

- 🧠 **What AI is** — learning from examples
- 📦 **Data** — features, labels, and bias
- 🐱 **Classification** — you trained a real model
- 📈 **Regression** — predicting numbers and the line of best fit
- 🌳 **Decision trees** — explainable yes/no logic
- ⚡ **Neural networks** — neurons, weights, and self-learning

That's a real foundation in how AI works — the same ideas pros use every day. Go build something amazing.
